name: Fictional customer - full SDLC sample

sdlc.current: Work starts while the issue's requirements and acceptance criteria are unclear.
sdlc.desired: Produce a verifiable brief through clarification questions.
Turn only the approved brief scope into an execution plan.

sdlc.current: Changes drift outside the plan scope and cause rework.
sdlc.desired: Implement minimal test-first changes within the plan scope.

sdlc.current: Test execution and result recording are inconsistent.
sdlc.desired: Record failing, passing, and regression test results as observed facts.

sdlc.current: Change intent and test evidence are separated, causing review gaps.
sdlc.desired: Read the implementation together with actual test results and report important defects with evidence.

sdlc.current: After review, publication responsibility and resume evidence are unclear.
sdlc.desired: An explicit human maintainer approves, then creates the PR through the existing process and provides the URL.

sdlc.current: The post-publication follow-up procedure is undocumented.
sdlc.desired: Keep the PR URL and reviewed-change match as resume evidence and mark remote status as unverified.

glossary.brief: A draft capturing the goal, scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria confirmed from the issue
glossary.plan: An execution plan including implementation files, verification methods, and stop conditions
glossary.implementation: The local changes made within the plan scope and their intent
glossary.test-results: The actually observed failing, passing, and regression test results
glossary.review-report: A read-only report separating requirements, defects, test evidence, and unverified items
glossary.pr-url: The URL of the PR the maintainer created manually and the reviewed-change confirmation

pains.description: Clarification, planning, implementation, review, and publication are disconnected, causing rework and publication incidents.
pains.impact: Scope changes repeatedly and publication responsibility is ambiguous.
pains.frequency: A fictional example; the real frequency is not confirmed.

success_criteria: Each stage's artifact moves to the next stage only after approval.
Publication happens only with the maintainer's prior approval and direct action.
Test results and resume evidence remain observed facts.
constraints: Fictional customer information; real tool access and permissions are not confirmed.
This sample does not perform automated publishing, merging, or deployment.

facts.statement: The sample content is fictional material for explaining product behavior.
facts.evidence: A development fixture included in the repository

assumptions: At run time the issue body is provided or approved local reads are available.
unknowns: The real customer's issue format, repository path, and approvers are not confirmed.
